name: Screen-space distortion
oneLiner: The finished picture bends like hot air, water and lenses: heat haze rising over fires, a slow wobble under water, a portal that swirls and pulls in what is behind it, and shockwave rings that refract the whole scene outward from an explosion, slam or kill. One WebGL pass on the I-08 pipeline that only moves where each pixel is read from; HUD rects never bend. Without WebGL, or with ?webgl=0, the game looks exactly as before.
fits: any browser game drawn on one 2D canvas, pixel or HD, any resolution and CSS scaling
action RPG, platformer, shmup, brawler (explosions, slams, kills)
levels with fire, lava, water or magic gates
notFor: games already drawn with WebGL or a 3D engine (use the engine's own post stack)
per-sprite effects that must follow a moving character pixel-exactly (it bends screen areas, not sprites)
colour changes: it moves pixels, it does not tint or light them (use grade, bloom or lights)

needs: I-08 webgl-post (GameDNA_Post) loaded first; the game's existing instance, or one the module creates
render() once per drawn frame on every draw path
the game's step-counted clock in ms (waves and ripples; deterministic ?t=&freeze=1)
optional: on-screen regions each frame (heat / water / portal, camera subtracted)
optional: explosion, slam, heavy-hit and kill events with an on-screen point (shockwave)
optional: HUD rects in canvas px or view units (uiRects), or the shared uiMask
provides: one distortion pass on the I-08 chain (order 350, the distortion band), skipped when idle
heat, water and portal regions; params.underwater for a whole level
shockwave(x, y, {strength}) rings fading in game time (max 8, same-spot merge)
HUD protection: uiRects with a feathered fade, never samples HUD pixels into the world
stats(): frames drawn, waves fired / live, regions, HUD rects, errors

assets: module/screen-distortion.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_Distort) adding one pass to an I-08 GameDNA_Post instance (shared or its own)
requires elements/webgl-post/module/webgl-post.js (I-08), shipped next to it in the combo

module.skin: optional: the shine tint may be a skin token (fx.hot) when skin-api.js is loaded; the module draws nothing on the game canvas
